messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a hosted-api p99 spike ~03:04 UTC. p99 ~920ms, baseline ~220ms. p95 climbed to 180ms. Dash: https://grafana/redwood/hosted-api
infra-bot: ALERT: hosted-api.p99 > 800ms (svc=hosted-api prod)
jamie: Thx. Any obvious correlation with deploys?
alex: No deploys in that window per deploy-bot. I started a quick profiler on one affected shard.
sophia: Shipping the profiler dump now. Main symptoms: queue depth increasing on the frontend worker, many small batches (avg batch size 3 -> 1.2), kernel selection toggling between aw-optimized and aux-fallback repeatedly.
mike: That batch size collapse smells like continuous batching timeout misfire or KV cache cache-miss storm. Any cache eviction logs?
alex: Pasted the runtime logs (trimmed):
```
[03:03:58] kvcache: evict tenant=acct-42 keys=210 policy=LFR
[03:03:58] batcher: sample_window=8ms avg_batch=3.1 -> 1.1
[03:03:59] kernel_selector: chosen=aw-optimized seq_len=64 -> fallback=aux-quantized
[03:03:59] prefetch: miss_rate=0.72 ramp=fast
[03:04:00] worker_queue: depth=42 -> 320
```
jamie: acct-42 again? They've been noisy earlier this month. Can we isolate?
lisa: I checked tenant routing — acct-42 traffic spiked ~5x at 03:02 UTC and their requests have large prompt prefixes that bust the KV cache working set. Prefetch miss amplifies batches to singletons.
sophia: Kernel selector oscillation note: when KV cache misses increase, sequence lengths vary and we hit a different kernel path; selector heuristics then flip back when a small spike of cache hits returns -> kernel thrashing. That adds CPU/GPU context-switch overhead and increases latency tail.
mike: Quick mitigation options: 1) rate-limit noisy tenant, 2) pin tenant to aux-quantized kernel to avoid oscillation, 3) bump coalesce window to 12ms to avoid tiny batches.
jamie: Can we do a fast pin to aux for acct-42 only? Would reduce perf but stabilize p99.
alex: I can patch routing rule for that tenant in ~4m. Rolling it for a single tenant should be safe.
infra-bot: Change request queued: route-update acct-42 -> aux-quantized (dry-run=false) by alex
lisa: Also, increase prefetch parallelism for the shard? If prefetch goes faster we might avoid miss ramp. But risky.
sophia: Prefer tenant pin + coalesce bump. Coalesce change is global and could affect latency for others; we should prefer a targeted tenant fix first.
mike: Agreed. Alex, flip the rule and watch queue depth + avg batch size. If p99 drops, revert plan B.
alex: Patching now. command:
```
redwood ctl route set --tenant acct-42 --kernel aux-quantized --reason "temp noisy tenant stabilization"
```
alex: Done. infra-bot shows rollout success on shard-7.
infra-bot: route-update acct-42 -> aux-quantized applied on shard-7 by alex (ok)
jamie: Post-change metrics?
alex: After pin: queue depth dropped 320 -> 45 over 30s, avg batch size went 1.2 -> 2.9, p99 dropping toward 240ms.
lisa: Nice. Any signs of eviction rate decreasing?
sophia: kvcache.evictions for shard-7 fell from 210/min -> 18/min. Kernel selector stable: chosen consistently aux-quantized, no thrash.
mike: Good. Next: open a short-lived play to see if we can tune coalesce window on a per-tenant basis. Also add a heuristic to kernel_selector to avoid flip-flopping if previous kernel had >Xms warmup cost.
jamie: I'll file a follow-up perf ticket with profiling traces and suggested selector change. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml.
alex: Action items from thread: 1) temporary pin acct-42 -> aux-quantized (done) 2) add per-tenant coalesce override (feature request) 3) kernel_selector: debounce flips (eng-ml) 4) run a replay of acct-42 traffic on staging with different prefetch configs (ops)
lisa: I'll monitor for collateral impact. Early signs look green.
infra-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: hosted-api.p99 returned to normal range (p99 < 400ms)
jamie: Thanks team. Adding postmortem notes and schedule a brief retro tomorrow.
sophia: I'll attach profiler dumps and kernel selector trace to the ticket.
mike: Optional: consider a short-term automated noisy-tenant throttle when evictions > threshold to avoid manual pins.
alex: Agree. Closing this thread — will follow up in the ticket. :thumbsup:
